reasons: The lake record is verified and identifies the input case as Florence v. County of Burlington, with canonical name Florence v. Board of Chosen Freeholders of County of Burlington.
The lake citations match the asserted official citation, parallel citations, neutral cite, court, and 2012 decision year.
The opinion frames the case as whether every detainee admitted to the general population may undergo a close visual inspection while undressed.
The Court rejected the proposed minor-offense/reasonable-suspicion exception and concluded the Fourth and Fourteenth Amendments do not require that framework.
Justice Alito's concurrence states the holding covers arrestees committed to the general population and visual strip searches not involving physical contact.
residual_risks: The most precise formulation should retain the no-physical-contact and general-population limitations.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Add that the visual strip search did not involve physical contact and applied to arrestees committed or being admitted to the general jail population.

reasons: The opinion repeatedly describes the challenged procedure as an intake search aimed at contraband, weapons, drugs, disease, and institutional security.
The asserted role is only Related (cross-doctrine), not a claim that Florence is an inventory-search holding.
residual_risks: No separate Inventory Searches home-page criteria were disclosed; this stands only as a cross-doctrine relation inferable from the intake/booking context.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Keep the role as Related (cross-doctrine); do not promote it to a key inventory-search authority.

defect.proposed_fix: Change the role to Related (cross-doctrine), or supply disclosed home-page criteria showing Florence is treated as a key progeny/refinement authority there.

residual_risks: No Special Needs and Administrative Searches home-page criteria were disclosed.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use Related (cross-doctrine) for this home unless the corpus has independent criteria for treating Florence as key there.
